children: China lost 38 stocks from MSCI's flagship global indexes in the November review and gained three, while Indonesia shed two more names and was allowed to add none.

The index provider published the results late on November 11, and the changes take effect at the close of November 30. Across the MSCI ACWI, 13 securities come in and 100 go out, so Chinese names make up more than a third of all deletions, according to the country lists. Indonesia loses Barito Pacific and Bumi Resources Minerals; the Philippines loses Manila Electric and PLDT.

The cut breaks a year of near-balance for China. In the three earlier reviews of 2026 its additions ran close to or ahead of its deletions, and in February they won 37 to 16. For Indonesia the direction is fixed in advance: MSCI has barred additions since January, and the country has now lost 11 standard-index constituents this year without gaining one. Passive funds tracking the benchmarks have until the end of the month to sell.
Additions to and deletions from the MSCI Global Standard Indexes for China and Indonesia, by quarterly review, 2026. Source: MSCI index review announcements. IntelliNews
China swaps consumer names for AI hardware

Mainland A-shares held through the Hong Kong Stock Connect account for 22 of the 38 Chinese deletions, among them CSI Solar, battery-materials maker CNGR Advanced Material, lithium miner Sinomine Resource and robot vacuum maker Ecovacs. Ganfeng Lithium's Hong Kong shares and developer Longfor go too. Thirteen deleted names, including dairy group China Feihe, Hengan, Miniso and Yadea, drop into MSCI's small-cap index rather than leaving the indexes altogether, which softens the selling.

The three additions point the other way. Optical module maker Zhongji Innolight, whose first-half profit rose 241.7% to CNY13.65bn ($2.05bn) on demand from AI data centres, enters with its Hong Kong-listed shares as the largest addition to the MSCI Emerging Markets Index. The review shifts the index towards AI suppliers and away from solar, lithium and consumer stocks, whose market values have fallen.

Barito Pacific falls out of both the standard and small-cap indexes, while Bumi Resources Minerals moves down to small caps. Seven other Indonesian companies, among them toll-road operator Jasa Marga and developer Ciputra, leave the small-cap index, and Indonesia will have seven standard-index stocks, down from nine. Nafan Aji Gusta, a senior analyst at Mirae Asset Sekuritas, estimated the passive outflow at IDR1.2 trillion ($65.8mn),

The sums are modest; the signal is not. MSCI put Indonesia's freeze in place over opaque shareholdings and suspected coordinated trading, and on October 15 opened a consultation on moving the market from emerging to standalone status, with a decision due by June 30, 2027. The proposal knocked the Jakarta Composite Index down more than 15% in two days. Until the freeze lifts, every review can only take Indonesian names out, and the resignation of Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has added political risk to the market's governance problem.

Indonesia's year has run from President Prabowo Subianto defying MSCI's demands and Fitch flagging companies exposed to the review, to Jakarta adding independent members to its share-ownership panel and investors eyeing Thailand as an alternative, with this week's two standard-index deletions as the latest instalment. For China the next test comes in February, when the AI names will need to keep their market values to keep their places.

title: MSCI drops 38 Chinese stocks, freezes Indonesia out in November review
